title: Zero Pack's Guide to Custom Compostable Packaging
subtitle: Choose the right packaging. Build a better brief. Make claims you can support.
tagline: A practical guide to choosing, planning and briefing custom compostable packaging that fits your products, brand and operation.
answerBox: The right custom compostable packaging should protect the product, work with your packing process, present your brand well and carry only the claims supported by its certification.
whatsInside: How to define the job your packaging must do
How to compare packaging types without forcing the wrong solution
How certification, disposal instructions and environmental claims fit together
What to prepare for artwork, quoting and production
A decision checklist and quote-ready planning worksheet

sections.heading: 1. Start with the job your packaging must do
sections.answerBox: Choose packaging around the product and delivery journey first. Material and branding decisions come after the functional brief is clear.
paragraphs: Good custom packaging begins with a clear job, not a product name. Before comparing materials or artwork, define what the packaging needs to protect, contain, carry or present.

Consider the entire journey: packing, storage, freight, handling, opening and disposal. Packaging that looks excellent but slows fulfilment, adds unnecessary space or fails in transit is not the right solution.

Zero Pack works across custom compostable packaging, with custom mailers as an important hero product rather than the limit of the range. Bring us the packaging problem, or a finished brief, and we can explore the right solution with you.
bullets: What is being packed, including weight, dimensions and any fragile, sharp, liquid or heat-sensitive features
Whether the packaging is for shipping, product protection, retail carry, garment protection, food contact or another purpose
How the packaging will be filled, sealed, stored and handled
Where it will be delivered and what conditions it may encounter
What the customer should do with it after use

sections.heading: 2. Compare packaging types
paragraphs: Custom compostable packaging can take many forms. The best choice depends on the product and the role the packaging plays, not which option happens to be most familiar.

A flexible mailer may be ideal for clothing or soft goods. A garment bag may be better for product protection inside a shipment. A carry bag serves a different purpose again. Fragile or structured products may need a padded or rigid solution.

Do not assume the certification or performance of one packaging type automatically applies to another. Construction, material, thickness, closures and additional layers can change what is possible and what evidence is required.
bullets: Shipping mailers: lightweight outer packaging for suitable non-fragile products
Garment bags: product protection and presentation for apparel
Shopping and carry bags: retail, events, campaigns and customer carry
Flexible bags and pouches: containment, presentation or product protection
Padded and protective packaging: added cushioning where product risk requires it
Layflat tubing: flexible lengths for variable products and packing processes
Rigid and food-related packaging: developed to the confirmed product, safety and manufacturing requirements

sections.heading: 3. Check product fit and protection
paragraphs: The smallest workable size is often a good starting point, but it must still allow the product to load, close and travel without putting the seams or closure under unnecessary stress.
Measure the packed product, not only the product on its own. Include folded garments, retail boxes, inserts, tissue or other items that will sit inside the packaging.

A packaging change should be tested against real handling conditions. Samples and prototypes can help confirm sizing, feel and pack-out, but final performance depends on the approved production specification.
bullets: Allow enough clearance for efficient packing and reliable closure
Check whether sharp corners or rigid edges could stress flexible material
Consider moisture exposure, compression, abrasion and temperature during transit
Avoid unnecessary empty space that increases material and freight volume
Test the full packed product where protection is business-critical

sections.heading: 4. Understand certification and claims
sections.answerBox: All Zero Pack compostable packaging is certified compostable.
paragraphs: Compostable, biodegradable, recyclable and plastic-free are not interchangeable terms. Each claim needs its own evidence, scope and customer guidance.

Recognised certification helps establish whether a product meets defined compostability requirements. Home-compostable and industrial-compostable certification relate to different conditions and should not be presented as the same thing.

All Zero Pack compostable packaging is certified compostable. Depending on the confirmed packaging and material, relevant schemes can include AS 5810, AS 4736, OK compost HOME and OK compost INDUSTRIAL. We confirm the certification that applies to each project.
Certification evidence should stay connected to the packaging it covers. A certificate for one material or product should not be treated as evidence for a different construction.
bullets: Name the exact certification only when it applies to the packaging being produced
Keep home- and industrial-compostable claims separate
Avoid vague claims such as eco-friendly unless the intended meaning is clearly explained and supported
Do not imply that certification guarantees acceptance by every council or processor
Confirm any certification mark and disposal wording before artwork is approved

sections.heading: 5. Separate certification from disposal guidance
paragraphs: Certification describes what a product has been tested and verified to do under defined conditions. Disposal guidance describes the pathway available to the customer in a particular place. They are related, but they are not the same question.

A certified product may not be accepted by a local kerbside organics service or commercial processor. Collection rules can depend on councils, contracts, contamination controls, infrastructure and the receiving facility.

Customer instructions should therefore match both the packaging evidence and the disposal pathway you can reasonably support. Where local rules vary, say so clearly rather than offering a universal bin instruction.
bullets: Confirm whether the packaging is certified for home or industrial composting
Check current local collection or processor guidance before naming a bin or service
Keep disposal instructions clear, visible and easy to follow
Avoid implying that compostable packaging will break down in general waste, recycling or the natural environment
Review instructions when selling into a new market

sections.heading: 6. Design packaging that looks like your brand
paragraphs: Custom packaging is a visible part of the customer experience. It should feel connected to the product and brand rather than like a generic item with a logo added at the end.

Start with a clear hierarchy: what should the customer notice first, what information must be easy to find and what can stay secondary? Leave enough space for required certification, disposal and production information.

Artwork requirements depend on the packaging, print method and production setup. Confirm the dieline, colour requirements, print limits, safe areas and file requirements before final artwork is prepared.
bullets: Use supplied production artwork templates rather than guessing dimensions
Keep logos and important copy within the approved safe area
Confirm colour references and understand that printed material can differ from a screen
Check small text, fine lines, reverses and barcodes at production size
Approve certification marks and disposal wording as part of the artwork review

sections.heading: 7. Plan quantities, budget and timing
paragraphs: Custom packaging is made for your order, so quantities, setup and freight are different from buying stock packaging. The right quantity balances unit economics with storage, cash flow, demand and the risk of artwork or product changes.

Custom compostable mailer orders start from 2,000 units, with the final minimum depending on size, print, material and specification. Other packaging types can have different minimums and should be confirmed for the project.

Production and delivery timing also depend on the approved packaging and freight plan. Work backwards from the date the packaging needs to be available and allow time for scoping, pricing, artwork, approval, production and delivery.
bullets: Use realistic order volumes rather than an aspirational forecast
Consider how many packaging sizes are genuinely needed
Allow for storage space and stock-management costs
Discuss destination, delivery method and required date early
Set a reorder point that reflects your actual production and freight plan

sections.heading: 8. Build a useful supplier brief
paragraphs: You do not need a finished technical specification before you ask for help. You do need enough information for the supplier to understand the product, packaging job and commercial context.
A strong brief reduces back-and-forth and makes it easier to compare options properly. If a detail is unknown, mark it as open rather than guessing.
bullets: Business name, website and destination market
Product description, dimensions, weight and protection needs
Current packaging and what you want to improve
Preferred packaging type, if known
Estimated quantity and likely reorder pattern
Brand colours, print expectations and artwork status
Certification or disposal requirements
Required delivery location and target date
Any food-contact, barrier, closure or operational requirements

sections.heading: 9. Decision checklist
paragraphs: Custom compostable packaging is likely to be worth exploring when you can define the packaging job, have repeat demand and want the finished result to support both practical and brand goals.
A 'not yet' answer is useful. It may mean testing a simpler packaging setup, reducing the number of sizes or waiting until demand is more predictable.
bullets: We understand what the packaging needs to do
We can estimate repeat demand with reasonable confidence
We have space and cash flow for custom-production quantities
We know which products and sizes need to fit
We can allow time for artwork, approval, production and delivery
We are prepared to use accurate certification and disposal wording
Our brand will benefit from a stronger packaging experience
We have someone who can own the project internally

sections.heading: 10. Quote-ready planning worksheet
paragraphs: Use the worksheet in the downloadable guide to turn what you know into a clear first conversation. Complete what you can and leave genuinely open decisions for discussion.
The aim is not to arrive with every answer. It is to give Zero Pack enough context to explore the right packaging and identify what must be confirmed next.
bullets: What are you packing?
What job must the packaging do?
What are the packed product dimensions and weight?
How many units do you expect to use?
Where will the packaging be delivered and used?
What do you want the customer to notice or understand?
What certification or disposal information is important?
When do you need the packaging?
Is artwork ready, in progress or not started?
What questions still need an expert answer?

faqs.question: Do I need a finished brief before contacting Zero Pack?
faqs.answer: No. Bring us the packaging problem, or a finished brief. Product details, likely quantities, destination and timing help us identify the next useful questions.

faqs.question: What is the minimum order quantity?
faqs.answer: Custom compostable mailer orders start from 2,000 units. The final minimum depends on size, print, material and specification. Minimums for other packaging types vary and are confirmed for the project.

faqs.question: Can Zero Pack help with packaging beyond mailers?
faqs.answer: Yes. Zero Pack is a custom compostable packaging specialist. Depending on the project, this can include shipping mailers, garment bags, shopping and carry bags, flexible bags and pouches, padded and protective packaging, layflat tubing, rigid packaging, food-related packaging and other custom solutions.

faqs.question: Can certification evidence be provided?
faqs.answer: Yes. Certification evidence can be provided on request after the relevant packaging and specification have been confirmed.

faqs.question: Does compostable mean it can go into any organics bin?
faqs.answer: No. Certification and local collection acceptance are separate. Check the packaging certification and the current guidance for the relevant council, collection service or processor before publishing a bin instruction.
